brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A herbal infusion from the young leaves of a small evergreen tree of the laurel family, not the tea plant, gathered in the Yinghua mountains of Shifang in Sichuan. It takes its name from Hongbai, one of the few townships where it is common.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Local people are said to have prepared it by their own home methods for over a thousand years, and farmers claim some trees are about 500 years old. It is still mostly collected from the wild, with very little cultivation. Little more is documented.
processing: Dried plant material, as with most herbal infusions.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: Described as having a distinctive, pleasant fragrance.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
